№ 01The blink

Them · the interviewer

“So why did you leave your last job?”

200ms

Between one person finishing and the next one starting, there are usually about 200 milliseconds. Researchers compared ten languages; it barely changes.

600ms

Yet getting from a thought to a spoken word takes 600 milliseconds or more.

So we start answering before they’ve finished asking.

InterviewHacker

InterviewHacker works the same way. While they’re still talking, it’s listening. When they stop, the answer starts to surface.

Sources: Stivers et al., 2009, PNAS; Levinson & Torreira, 2015, Frontiers in Psychology.

Until someone asks you,it stays quiet.

Most of a stand-up isn’t addressed to you. It takes notes quietly and offers a line only when the question is yours. Want silence all the way through? Switch to Record only.

11:00Round two·backend

  1. Round 1Oct 22 · reviewed
  3. Round 2today · continued

When the database and the cache both change, how do you keep them consistent?

Write the database first, then delete the cache. Failed deletes go to a retry queue, and a binlog subscriber deletes again as a backstop.

What tripped you in round one,it remembers in round two.

Round two picks up where round one left off: the material, the review and the better answers come along. When the follow-up lands, the answer surfaces word by word. Shorter, an example, the other language: one tap.

14:00Lab meeting·in person

How did you choose the control group?

Stratified by age and baseline, then drawn at random. Details on page 4, table 2.

Same room,same help.

In person it listens through the microphone alone: the whole room on one line, marked In the room. In person it records by default; ask it to answer and it works from the paper you added, page number included.

16:30Client call·sharing your whole screen

Can we go live by the end of the month?

Sharing your whole screen?Keep the answer on your phone.

Share only the meeting window and they never see your prompts. Sharing everything? Hand the answer to your phone: scan a pairing code with its camera and the page that opens is your prompter. No app to install.

Conversations don’t wait for you to be ready.

An interviewer’s follow-up, left hanging.

Your advisor: “And the control group?”

Across the table: “Another eight percent.”

In class, your name, out of nowhere.

On the line: “Live by month-end?”

The last question at your defence.

Each one gives you a blink.

21:40

After the call · notes

After the call,
the same page becomes the notes.

Answers during the call are about speed; notes are not. Press End and it works through the call at its own pace: misheard words fixed from context, every point tied to the moment it was said, nothing written that nobody said, anything unclear marked To confirm.

№ 03Privacy22:30

Your voice stays on this Mac.

  1. i.

    Heard on this Mac.

    What they say and what you say becomes text right here, by default.

  2. ii.

    No recordings.

    Only the transcript and the notes remain, and you can delete them.

  3. iii.

    You decide who gets what.

    The text needed for answers and notes goes only to the service you choose.

No stealth promises: get consent from everyone present before recording or transcribing, and follow the rules of the meeting.

№ 04FAQ23:10

Asked often.

01Will the other side know I’m using it?

It sends nothing into the meeting; it only shows on your screen or phone. If you share your whole screen, prompts on it can be seen, so move the answer to your phone. Whether and how you use it, follow the rules of the meeting.

02Does it work with any meeting app?

Yes. It listens to the sound your Mac plays, so it doesn’t need to know which app that is.

03What if we’re all in one room?

Choose In person. It uses only the microphone and marks the transcript In the room.

04Does it keep recordings?

No. Speech becomes text on your Mac; only the transcript and notes remain.

05I only want notes, no interruptions.

PressRecord now. It takes notes quietly during the meeting, and the notes are on the page when it ends.

06When can I use it?

The first beta is running now. Join the waitlist and we’ll write to you as soon as places open.
